title: Luis Federico Leloir's birth chart
metaDescription: Luis Federico Leloir's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 13.0° Virgo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun and Neptune sit 0.8° from an exact sextile — near enough that the tradition reads identity and imagination as a single working part. Sextiles are read as standing invitations — productive exactly as often as they are accepted.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Virgo, but precisely: 13.0°, second decan, 10°–20°, under Saturn in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Day to day the chart speaks through Mercury in Leo (27.6°), Venus in Libra (28.8°), Mars in Leo (26.2°): a mind that decides at speaking speed, taste led by wit and proportion, drive that ignites on contact.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Saturn to Neptune is the closest call of the day, a trine within 0.7°. A trine runs downhill — the talent that never announces itself because it never had to. Behind it, the Sun sextile Neptune at 0.8°, and Mercury sextile Venus at 1.2° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Two planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. Venus in Libra at 28.8° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Jupiter in Cancer at 6.8° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 3 in water, 2 in earth, 2 in fire, 2 in air by element, 4 cardinal, 3 mutable, 2 fixed by modality. A water emphasis keeps long books: little is forgotten, and nothing is felt only once. Saturn and Uranus were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Aries into Taurus during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.4° between one midnight and the next. Without a recorded hour there is no honest way to say which side it was on, so this reading does not say. The Moon sign is a real question here, not a rounding error, and it needs a birth time nobody has published.
